items.corrected_text: On 29 September 2025 Kassel's city parliament approved a large expansion of paid parking (Parkgebührenzone II), with the CDU, FDP and Greens coalition voting in favour and AfD, SPD and Left against. The new rules were to take effect in May 2026; resident permits rise from a maximum of EUR 30 to EUR 110 a year, and the city expected about EUR 3 million extra revenue a year.
items.corrected_title: Ausweitung der Parkzonen in Kassel: Doppelt so groß, dreimal so teuer (hessenschau.de)

Facts check out (published 30.04.26: about 300 meters existing, 368 new, 'sukzessive' from 1 May, area more than doubles by July, step by step per district; EUR 1/hour or EUR 6/day for non-residents; EUR 110 flat instead of max EUR 30; businesses and freelancers have no claim to special permits). The 'roughly 300 to 668' total is arithmetic (300+368) not stated on the page. source_title is wrong: the real title is 'In Kassel wird Parken ab Mai teurer - und für viele schwieriger'; the 'Parkgebührenzone ab Mai mehr als verdoppelt:' prefix is not on the page. items.corrected_text: From 1 May 2026 Kassel is extending its paid on-street parking zones: 368 new parking meters are added to the roughly 300 existing ones (about 668 in total), and the fee-charging area more than doubles by July 2026, introduced step by step from district to district. Non-residents pay EUR 1 per hour or EUR 6 per day; resident permits are a flat EUR 110 a year (previously max. EUR 30). Businesses and freelancers have no claim to special permits.
items.corrected_title: In Kassel wird Parken ab Mai teurer - und für viele schwieriger (hessenschau.de)

items.corrected_text: The city's resident-parking FAQ states that the expanded zone II covers streets in Bad Wilhelmshöhe, Nord-Holland, Rothenditmold, Südstadt, Unterneustadt, Vorderer Westen, Wehlheiden and Wesertor. Permits could be applied for from 1 April 2026 and 1 May 2026 was set as the earliest effective date; the expansion was rolled out in phases, starting in Vorderer Westen and Wehlheiden, with further areas there and in Bad Wilhelmshöhe from June 2026, and the page now says the new rules have applied in Südstadt, Unterneustadt, Wesertor and Rothenditmold since July.

items.note: Figures match the slides: fees up about 60% after the 2014 change, 400% on 60 of about 11,000 spaces in Zentrum (Markthalle area), revenue EUR 4,633,451 (2013) and EUR 7,051,909 (2015), long-term parkers displaced into car parks. But the document is a presentation by the Amt 66 (Straßenverkehrs- und Tiefbauamt, G. Förster) for the SPD faction motion 101.18.41, dated 29.09.2016, not a 'Bericht des Magistrats'; the draft title is the file name, not the document title ('Überprüfung der Parkgebührenordnung').
items.corrected_text: A city-office presentation (Amt 66) dated 29 September 2016, prepared in response to an SPD-faction motion to review the 2014 Parkgebührenordnung, said the 2014 change raised parking fees by about 60% (and by 400% on 60 of roughly 11,000 spaces in the Zentrum zone). Parking-fee revenue was EUR 4.63 million in 2013 and EUR 7.05 million in 2015. The city noted long-term parkers had been displaced into the multi-storey car parks, improving chances for short-stay street parkers.
items.corrected_title: Überprüfung der Parkgebührenordnung (Antrag der SPD-Fraktion 101.18.41), presentation of 29 September 2016

items.note: Parkgebührenordnung page: 'Vom 19. Mai 2014 in der Fassung der Dritten Änderung vom 29. September 2025', amendment in force 1 May 2026; EVs marked as such pay no fee with a parking disc, exemption ends at end of 31 Dec 2026 - correct. The FAQ claim is inaccurate: the FAQ says holders of e-vehicles in new resident zones do not need a permit because e-vehicles may park free 'bis auf Weiteres' (until further notice); the 31 Dec 2026 date in the FAQ applies to paid short-stay bays (3 h with parking disc) and is tied to the Elektromobilitätsgesetz, whose extension is unpredictable.
items.corrected_text: Under Kassel's Parkgebührenordnung (third amendment of 29 September 2025, effective 1 May 2026), electric vehicles marked as such pay no fee when using a parking disc; this exemption ends at the end of 31 December 2026. The resident-parking FAQ adds that holders of e-vehicles in the new resident-parking zones do not need a permit because e-vehicles may park fee-free until further notice, while on paid short-stay bays (up to 3 hours with a parking disc) the free parking applies until 31 December 2026 because it is tied to the Elektromobilitätsgesetz.

items.corrected_text: On 10 November 2022 five council factions (Greens, SPD, CDU, Left and FDP) and several individual councillors filed a joint resolution (101.19.658) backing the retention of the GALERIA store at Obere Königsstraße/Opernplatz, asking the magistrate to press the group's management to avert closure of the Kassel site.

corrected_summary: Kassel's biggest recent parking change is the expansion of paid zone II from 1 May 2026 (approved by the city parliament on 29 September 2025): 368 new meters were added to roughly 300 existing ones, the paid area more than doubles by July 2026, and resident permits cost a flat EUR 110 a year instead of at most EUR 30, with the city expecting about EUR 3 million extra revenue a year. Electric vehicles with a parking disc park fee-free until 31 December 2026. In the centre the Garde du Corps car park (reported as 360-380 spaces) has been closed since October 2024 and is to be demolished, and a lane on Untere Königsstraße was converted to outdoor dining in March 2025 for a one-year trial. Garages are run by the city, the Parkhausgesellschaft der Stadt Kassel and Apcoa, and demand drivers include documenta 16 (12 June-19 September 2027) and Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe, where parking is often full on water-show days.
